title: Exact three-column constellation conjecture
statement:
Let $T(n,k)$ be the largest number of points in an $n$ by $k$ regular grid such that no three selected points form an isosceles triangle of nonzero area. **Three-column exact-value conjecture.** For $n>4$,

$$
T(n,3)=n+1\quad\text{if }n\text{ is odd},
$$

and

$$
T(n,3)=n+2\quad\text{if }n\text{ is even}.
$$

The preceding lemma establishes the corresponding lower bounds, but the supplied text gives no matching upper-bound proof or resolution, so the exact-value conjecture remains open here.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.00180

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).
source_name: Chai Wah Wu, “Counting the number of isosceles triangles in rectangular regular grids”, arXiv:1605.00180 (2017).
